text:
### Observed differences

- Three activities that formed a recurring middle segment nearly disappeared: A19, A20 and A21 each ran in about 30–36 in 100 traces in the earlier window (60–71 of 200), almost always followed directly by A29 (about 97–99% of their outgoing flow); in the later window each appears in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]
- Three activities took their place at scale: A26 and A27 were not observed at all in the earlier window and A28 in only 1 of 200 traces, while in the later window each runs about once in every trace (200 of 200 traces; about 1.0 occurrence per trace). [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- A44 now routes into the new group: earlier about 76 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A19, A20 or A21 (about 24–27% each) and about 23% to A10; later about 93 in 100 go to A26, A27 or A28 (about 30–33% each) and only about 2% to A10. [DIR009]
- The new group has no fixed internal order: from each of A26, A27 and A28 the outgoing flow splits roughly equally between the other two and A29 (about 31–37% each), which fits all three running once per trace in any order; A29 now follows A28 after 1–3 steps in similar shares rather than immediately. [DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, LAG003]
- The span from A44 to A29 lengthened: earlier A29 followed A44 within 2–3 steps in about 99 in 100 cases (about 75% at 2 steps); later it follows within 4–5 steps in all cases (about 90% at 4 steps, about 11% at 5). [LAG005]
- The new activities occupy the same region of the trace the old ones did: A26–A28 sit at about 0.38 of the trace length on average, where A19–A21 previously sat at about 0.36–0.37; A28 itself moved from a single earlier observation near the trace end (0.97) into this region. [POS005, POS006, POS007, POS002, POS003, POS004]
- A10 became rarer and less pointed: it ran in about 26 in 100 traces earlier versus about 11 in 100 later, and its outgoing flow shifted from mostly A21, A19 and A20 (about 40%, 26%, 19%) to a spread over many successors, the largest being A27 (about 17%) and A15 (about 13%). [OCC001, DIR001]
- A29 still runs in every trace in both windows and only shifted slightly later (mean relative position about 0.40 to 0.44). [POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A44 and A29 was restructured: in the earlier window A44 was followed by one of the alternatives A19, A20 or A21, each leading almost directly to A29, whereas in the later window A19–A21 are nearly unobserved and A26, A27 and A28 instead each run once in every trace between A44 and A29, in no fixed order among themselves, before A29. Participation (about 30–36 in 100 traces down to about 0; 0 up to 200 in 200), the rerouting of A44, the matching trace positions and the lengthened A44→A29 gap from 2–3 to 4–5 steps all show this directly and consistently. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR009, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, POS005, POS006, POS007, LAG005]

This body of evidence goes well beyond what sampling noise produces: 29 control-flow items qualified where fewer than one (about 0.59) would be expected for an unchanged process, so the differences as a whole cannot be explained by random re-splits of a stable process. [OCC002, OCC005, DIR009, LAG005]

Limitations: the later-window behaviour of A19, A20 and A21 rests on a single observed trace each, so their remaining routing is essentially unobserved, and the evidence cannot show whether the old activities were removed from the process or only ceased to be triggered. A competing reading the evidence cannot fully rule out is that A26–A28 were introduced at a different point of the process while A19–A21 disappeared for a separate reason, although the matching positions and the longer A44→A29 distance favour the reading above. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS005, POS006, LAG005]

Other differences: A10 declined beyond its role in the earlier routing — from about 26 in 100 traces to about 11 in 100 — and its outgoing flow spread from A19/A20/A21 across many activities, largest A27 and A15; this rests on 53 versus 23 traces and is tentative. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001] A14 still leads almost always to A15 (about 99% versus 93%), with only a few rare new successors appearing. [DIR002]
